distributed generation can both increase and decrease the electrical energy technical losses of a distribution network, depending on the penetration levels, the power factors of the distributed sources and the location of these distributed sources in the network.

distributed generation can have a positive or negative impact on distribution network losses, depending on the power factor of the generation and the location of distributed generation in the distribution system.
the penetration level and the location of DGs have a great impact on the technical losses of distribution systems, but the power factor does not have any significant influence.

the penetration of DG in the distribution systems can be a double-edged sword, as it can both increase and decrease the distribution network technical loss levels, and therefore it is necessary to have an appropriate planning of the distributed generation penetration, in order to minimize the impact of the generation of losses in the distribution systems.
